notes: Focused on the Nouvelle Athenes / quartier Saint-Georges area of the 9th arrondissement (Square d'Orleans, rue de la Tour-des-Dames, Cite Malesherbes, rue de la Victoire, Cite Bergere), which is the classic Restauration/Louis-Philippe-era residential development in Paris and gives the cleanest surviving examples of flat plastered facades, incised refends, and thin lozenge/palmette wrought-iron balcony work from this period. Construction years are NOT stated in any of the source Commons descriptions (only photograph dates are, where given), so 'year' is left blank throughout per instructions rather than guessed; general art-historical knowledge places most of these ensembles in the 1820s-1830s (Square d'Orleans c.1829, Cite Bergere c.1825, rue de la Tour-des-Dames c.1820-1825, Cite Malesherbes c.1830s-40s) but this is NOT recorded per-image as fact since the sources themselves don't state it. Several other candidates were rejected as wrong-period: a brick/stone neo-Louis-XIII revival building at 11 rue de la Tour-des-Dames, and an elaborately sculpted Belle Epoque facade at 10 rue Chaptal (SACEM building), both clearly post-Haussmann in style despite being in the same streets. Two Cite Bergere shopfront-entrance photos and one Cite Malesherbes gardien-door photo were also rejected for being dominated by modern storefronts/hedges rather than legible period facade. Coverage is decent but concentrated in the 9th arrondissement; broader geographic spread (e.g. Marais, Faubourg Saint-Germain Restauration-era buildings) was not found in a legible, correctly-dated form during this search pass.
